title: Unitary state structure
competency: Define state structure and the unitary state, with its features, advantages and disadvantages.

keywords.def: How power is distributed among the parts of a state: unitary, federal or confederal.
A state structure where power is centralized: one central government controls all government.

en.text: State structure is how power is shared among the parts of a state. There are three: unitary, federal and confederal. A unitary state centralizes power: the central government controls everything and lower units act only by its will. It gives uniform administration and avoids conflict of authority, but concentrates power and may ignore local diversity.

screens.title: Family Z
screens.ask: In family "Z", the father decides everything and even teenage children cannot decide anything. Is power shared or concentrated?
screens.after: Concentrated. This is like a unitary state, where all power is at the centre.

screens.title: State structures
paras: State structure is the distribution of power among the parts of a state.
It asks whether power is devolved by the constitution to lower units or kept at the centre.
There are three: unitary, federal and confederal.
No structure is automatically democratic or undemocratic.

screens.title: The unitary state
paras: A unitary state centralizes power in one central government.
Executive, legislative and judicial powers are concentrated at the centre.
It may delegate powers, but by its own will, not by law.
table: Sovereignty lies only at the centre
screens.note: Examples in the book: China, Sri Lanka, the UK, France, Finland, Italy, Kenya, South Africa, Djibouti. Figure 2.1: power flows one way, from the centre down.
